items.author: Gumaro Rendon

items.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
items.summary: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.
items.author: Nada Khogeer, Jerison Parra, Caroline Desgranges, Hugo Ribeiro

items.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
items.summary: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.
items.author: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, David P. DiVincenzo et al.

items.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
items.summary: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.
items.author: Ghansham Chandel, Siddhartha Das

items.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
items.summary: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.
items.author: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell, Alessio Celi

items.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
items.summary: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.
items.author: Nathan McLane, Richard C. Remsing, Leah G. Dodson

items.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
items.summary: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Rényi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.
items.author: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

items.title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
items.summary: Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of determin
items.author: Soumyajyoti Chatterjee, Harishankar Mishra, Asvija Balasubramanyam, S D Sudarsan et al.

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications. To achieve this, we build a quantum program library in the Lean theorem prover in which large language model agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost. Agent teams collaborate, sharing results and knowledge through wikis and discussing ideas at organized conferences. Our results improve on prior baselines for parallel search (up to 1.4x), quantum arithmetic (290x), and simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x respectively. Combining human and artificial intelligence at scale, under the rigor of mathematical proof, lets researchers design algorithms that today's classical and quantum computers cannot test, shortening the path to practical quantum computation.
items.author: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova, George Tsoukalas et al.

items.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
items.summary: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. The measured distributions resolve both regimes and agree closely with quantum-trajectory theory. The crossover persists in interacting many-particle systems: the optimal monitoring point is preserved while many-body interference reshapes the distributions. Zeno suppression likewise persists in two-dimensional geometry. Together, these results show that the two regimes are a generic feature of monitored propagation rather than a single-particle effect. To our knowledge, our work constitutes the first experimental measurement of arrival-time distributions in a monitored quantum transport setting, addressing one of the longest-standing problems in quantum mechanics.
items.author: Yousef Mafi, K. G. S. H. Gunawardana, Kim Pöyhönen, Teemu Ojanen

items.title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
items.summary: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+Ω(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.
items.author: Yuan Deng, Zihan Hao, Honghao Lin, Qipeng Liu et al.

items.title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
items.summary: Quantum technologies based on individually controlled atoms are among the most promising platforms for scalable quantum computing, owing to their favorable coherence properties and controllability. Nonetheless, achieving reliable and high-fidelity gate operations remains challenging due to the sensitivity of these systems to noise and hardware imperfections. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive software toolset designed to model atomic quantum systems with high precision and simulate qubit gate dynamics. By integrating quantum optimal control and benchmarking techniques with automatic differentiation for efficient and accurate gradient-based optimization, the toolset enables significant improvements in gate performance. We demonstrate its capabilities through detailed case studies involving both neutral atoms and trapped ions, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing quantum gate fidelities, and providing valuable insights for experimental implementation.
items.author: Marco Rossignolo, Lorena C. Bianchet, Anurag Saha Roy, Shai Machnes

items.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
items.summary: Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that every bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. They showed that the conjecture implies that the acceptance probability of every quantum algorithm making $T$ queries can be approximated on most inputs by a classical algorithm making $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ queries. We prove their conjecture: every function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ of degree at most $d\ge1$ has a variable of influence at least $c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^{6}$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. In the original formulation, for polynomials of degree at most $d$ with values in $[0,1]$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ and variance at least $\varepsilon$, this gives a variable of influence at least $(\varepsilon/d)^{7}$. The proof is elementary, with steps inspired by works of others. Thus, as Aaronson and Ambainis anticipated, superpolynomial quantum speedups in the query model require structure, such as a promise on the inputs.
items.author: David Turturean

items.title: Long-range spectral entanglement and quantum correlations in highly nondegenerate multi-comb and ultrafast systems
items.summary: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single-comb systems for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum-enhanced spectroscopy. However, the production of bright quantum light across multiple nondegenerate pulses or frequency combs, a key technology for multispectral applications, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore a mechanism that generates a series of nonlinearly coupled bright frequency combs through cascaded three-wave upconversion and downconversion processes mediated by a single idler comb. We consider both discrete combs and broadband ultrafast pulse systems, showing how these systems generate inter- and intracomb two-mode squeezing and entanglement directly in the frequency basis, spanning a large spectral range. Furthermore, we demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to produce target cluster states and concentrated two-mode squeezing through covariance matrix optimization. Our findings uncover a new multimode quantum regime enabled by hierarchical nonlinear interactions in two frequency dimensions, unlocking applications such as entanglement-assisted spectroscopy, squeezing-enhanced pump-probe measurements, quantum spectral multiplexing, and spectrally addressable cluster state generation for quantum information science.
items.author: Sahil Pontula, Debasmita Banerjee, Marin Soljacic A, Yannick Salamin

items.title: Extending AIMNet2 to Macrocyclic Peptides through Data-Efficient Continual Training
items.summary: Abstract Macrocyclic peptides are among the most promising therapeutic modalities, yet no general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) has been systematically benchmarked for their conformational analysis. We show that on the MPCONF196 macrocyclic benchmark, the four-model AIMNet2 ensemble outperforms MACE-OFF23(S), despite macrocycles being entirely absent from its training data. A single AIMNet2 model is 3- to 5-fold faster and needs 5- to 63-fold less GPU memory than the MACE-OFF23 models at their default float64-precision. The four-model ensemble is about as fast as MACE-OFF23 but retains a 3- to 32-fold memory advantage even against MACE-OFF23 in float32. The larger MACE-OFF23(M) and MACE-OFF23(L) models remain more accurate. To narrow this gap, we introduce a continual training protocol that requires new quantum-chemical labels for fewer than 25,000 domain-specific conformers (<0.13% of the training corpus) while preserving conformational-energy accuracy on nonmacrocyclic molecules. On a sequence-disjoint holdout of unseen CREMP macrocyclic peptides, the resulting model, AIMNet2-macro, reduces conformational energy RMSE by 25 to 27% and DFT force RMSE by 20% (25% on backbone atoms) and improves lowest-energy conformer recovery relative to the original AIMNet2. It retains the conformational-energy accuracy of the original model on the nonmacrocyclic drug-like molecules of CONFORGE and also improves accuracy on the structurally distinct macrocycles of MPCONF196, although this smaller improvement is not statistically significant. Among the ten training strategies compared, only continual training on the combined corpus (AIMNet2-macro) achieves this improvement without degrading small-molecule accuracy. AIMNet2-macro is therefore the best balanced, tho
items.source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
items.author: Runtian Gao, R.I. Zubatyuk, Olexandr Isayev

items.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
items.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.
items.author: Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian, Andreas Bauer

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs. The evidence shows that distillation can improve selected quantum students, but benefits are task- and architecture-dependent, and several studies find negligible gains or even performance degradation. Evaluations on physical quantum hardware remain limited, with some testing individual quantum components rather than complete learning pipelines. Heterogeneous protocols and incomplete resource reporting prevent general conclusions about practical quantum advantage. We identify priorities for controlled benchmarking, noise-aware learning, reproducible evaluation, and efficient transfer between quantum and classical models.
items.author: Aldana Al-Sulaiti, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Muhammad Bilal Akram Dastagir, Ahmed Farouk et al.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. Quantum emitters were found in BNNTs spanning the entirety of the visible spectrum, including spectral regions where SPEs within hBN have not been reported. Furthermore, each tube was found to possess multiple SPEs at varying emission wavelengths along the length, exhibiting lifetimes as fast as 0.5 ns, which is about two-fold faster than the fastest hBN SPEs. Additionally, we demonstrate that surface passivation/coating mitigates blinking events, therefore increasing the emitter stability. Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.
items.author: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie, Dakota Braaten et al.

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.
items.author: Chenwei Lv

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth. Our bounds for Fock-state boson sampling cover both dilute and saturated regimes and become stronger near full input filling: when only a bounded number of input modes are empty, the noisy output for Haar-random interferometers converges, as the number of modes grows, to a distribution independent of the interferometer.
items.author: Armando Angrisani, Hela Mhiri

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation. Evaluation with a separately trained solubility prediction model showed that the best QNN and QKAN configurations achieved mean predicted solubility scores 14.0% and 22.7% higher than the multilayer perceptron (MLP) baseline, respectively. Experimental characterization further demonstrated biological activity across three distinct protein families. Selected defensins exhibited pronounced inhibitory activity against Aspergillus niger, while xylanases and short-chain dehydrogenases exhibited substantial enzymatic activity. Together, these results support DiffSequence-Q as a framework for integrating structural requirements and solubility targets in protein generation, with experimentally demonstrated biological activity.
items.author: Ke-Xin Tang, Zhen-Qiang Weng, Kai Yan, Yao-Yao Lu et al.

items.title: Quantum enhanced beam displacement estimation: sensitivity limits, optimal probes, and measurement schemes
items.summary: We investigate the ultimate sensitivity limits for measuring small transverse beam displacements and identify optimal strategies that attain them, using the framework of mode parameter estimation. We contrast two families of states with different resource constraints, using Hermite-Gauss and Laguerre-Gauss mode pairs. First, for fixed total photon number states, the optimal state is identified and we show that it asymptotically approaches a rotated NOON state. The sensitivity bound is compared to that of an asymptotically optimal pure Gaussian state with fixed average photon number. Finally, we propose concrete measurement schemes using the method of moments and show that the twin-Fock state may provide a viable alternative to the rotated NOON state for this task. Our work provides a broader benchmark for developing practical strategies for spatial sensing at the quantum limit.
items.author: Balázs Novák, Pau Colomer, Joseph Zhang, Emre Köse et al.

items.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
items.summary: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain. It requires only the chain geometry and the particle number. At strong dephasing, the density dynamics maps to a resistor chain, and an exact inverse-generator identity links the residual overlap to the spatial resistance profile. We find two distinct thresholds: a finite mean resistance suffices for diffusion, but the residual overlap decays as $L^{-1/2}$ with chain length $L$ only when the resistance variance is finite; rare weak links slow this decay. We predict the fraction of samples in which the blind preparation wins, which is an ensemble-level measure of its reliability. Finite-size calculations support both scaling regimes with interactions at strong dephasing. We give preparation circuits and a density readout for the residual overlap.
items.author: M Nishanth, Shreyas Sadugol, Payman Mahmoudi, Alexander Yosifov et al.

items.title: Recalibration-Aware Optimization of ZEFOZ Operating Points in $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ for Quantum Memories
items.summary: Erbium-doped solids like $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}:\mathrm{Y}_2\mathrm{SiO}_5$ have properties that make them suitable for quantum-network memories, however, their unquenched effective electronic spin causes rapid magnetic decoherence. Operating at Zero First-Order Zeeman (ZEFOZ) points allows us to mitigate this, where we evaluate the ZEFOZ landscape for Site-2 $^{167}\mathrm{Er}^{3+}$ by incorporating a full-Hessian spin-Hamiltonian treatment with the anisotropic magnetic-field covariance derived from the native $^{89}\mathrm{Y}$ crystal lattice directly. Operating-point screening criteria were adopted to devise a Pareto-optimal frontier of four transition pairs to balance modeled Y-only magnetic pure-dephasing lifetimes ($T_{φ,Y}^{(2)}$) against microwave control authority. The $ε_{14}\leftrightarrowε_{15}$ transition exhibits the longest modeled Y-bath-induced quadratic pure-dephasing time, $T_{φ,Y}^{(2)}>2.2\times10^5~\mathrm{s}$, while the $ε_{12}\leftrightarrowε_{13}$ transition stood out, achieving a Rabi frequency coefficient of $1.248 \times 10^5~\mathrm{Hz/mT}$. An assumption-based Hamiltonian-uncertainty analysis demonstrates that while uncompensated deviations shift the ZEFOZ condition away from its nominal magnetic-field coordinate, the shifted operating points can be recovered via numerical vector-field recalibration. The Pareto-optimal coordinates were mathematically recovered for all sampled Hamiltonian perturbations, and the $84.1^{\mathrm{st}}$-percentile field relocations ranged from $10.95$ to $27.97~\mathrm{mT}$. The intended operation near $10~\mathrm{mK}$ must be taken into account for the suppression of Er-induced spectral diffusion through electronic-spin polarization, while the extended Y-bath pure-dephasing timescales also remain conditional on
items.author: Shashank Srivastava

items.title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
items.summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.
items.author: Frank Göhmann, Karol K. Kozlowski, Mikhail D. Minin, Alexander Weiße

items.title: Atomic Static Electric Quadrupole Polarizability from Relativistic Many-Body Theory With Application To Thulium $\left(6s^2\, 4f^{13}\right)$\, $^2F_{7/2}$ and $^2F_{5/2}$
items.summary: In the present work a method for calculating atomic static electric rank-$n$ tensor quadrupole polarizabilities $α_Q^{(n)}(J)$ for arbitrary atomic electronic structure is presented. It is based on a linear-symmetry representation of atomic states using large-scale relativistic configuration interaction wavefunctions, and the quadrupole polarizabilities are obtained by a sum-over-states approach. The major result from applying this method to atomic thulium is $α_Q^{(0)}(\frac{7}{2}) = 2496^{+0}_{-231}$ \au for the electronic ground term $^2F_{7/2}$ static electric scalar quadrupole polarizability which is roughly a factor of four smaller than same property in the electronic ground state of the cesium atom. This finding adds to the favorable properties of thulium atoms in atomic-clock research.
items.author: Timo Fleig

items.title: Testing Gravitationally-Induced-Entanglement with Massive Particles and Quantum Clocks
items.summary: We present an experimental proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks. By harnessing the collective interaction between a micrometer-scale particle and an array of ultra-precise nuclear clocks, our scheme offers a conceivable path to observing gravitationally mediated entanglement with quantum clocks in the laboratory. Crucially, this setup will probe a genuinely relativistic effect one that requires the contribution of internal clock energy to active gravitational mass and cannot arise from the Newtonian interaction between fixed masses. Therefore, observing this entanglement would provide evidence for the quantised nature of active gravitational mass -- which has not been tested in any prior experiment -- rather than for spatial coherence of fixed masses,which is routinely tested in matterwave interferometers
items.author: Germain Tobar, Markus Aspelmeyer, Magdalena Zych

items.title: Quantum alternating operator ansatz beyond low depth with gradually changing unitaries
items.summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm and its generalization to Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOA) is a promising approach for applying quantum computers to challenging problems such as combinatorial optimization and computational chemistry. In this paper, we study the underlying mechanisms governing the behavior of QAOA circuits beyond shallow depth in the practically relevant setting of gradually varying unitaries. We use the discrete adiabatic theorem, which complements and generalizes the insights obtained from the continuous-time adiabatic theorem primarily considered in prior work. Our analysis explains some general properties that are conspicuously depicted in the recently introduced QAOA performance diagrams. For parameter sequences derived from continuous schedules (e.g. linear ramps), these diagrams capture the algorithm's performance over different parameter sizes and circuit depths. Surprisingly, they have been observed to be qualitatively similar across different performance metrics and application domains. Our analysis explains this behavior as well as entails some unexpected results, such as connections between the eigenstates of the cost and mixer QAOA Hamiltonians changing based on parameter size and the possibility of reducing circuit depth without sacrificing performance.
items.author: Vladimir Kremenetski, Anuj Apte, Tad Hogg, Stuart Hadfield et al.

items.title: Fast, Long-Range Synchronization Utilizing Emergents: Proof of Concept and Prospective Applications of Emergent Computing
items.summary: So far, synchronization tasks designed in complex systems are working at the level of their constituting elements. The proposed pilot study explores synchronization at the level of emergents. The main objective of this research is threefold: (i) to demonstrate that synchronizing emergent structures rise from a continuous interaction of micro-processes that are operating above a constituting matrix (medium) using a simple microevolution rule and a special type of extended neighborhood; (ii) to provide a specific example of a long-range emergent coordination that is generated within a short-range communicating medium; and (iii) to demonstrate a possibility of synchronization at the level of emergents. Those goals are achieved by the utilization of emergent information processing that uses uniform changes of all updated elements of the matrix, a fixed microevolution rule, and a fixed neighborhood. A fast solution to a computational problem of solving long-range synchronization within massively parallel and short-range communicating environments is presented. It is named the semi-two-dimensional synchronization problem (S2D-SP). The proposed emergent solution of S2D-SP differs from all previous manually designed solutions to other synchronization tasks. The number of steps t, which is necessary to synchronize an emergent array, is substantially lower than the width w of the synchronized emergent array. In addition to the pure theoretical importance, the solution demonstrates the usefulness of the concept of extended neighborhoods in search of not only biologically relevant computational models of self-organization and emergence. The presented solution of the S2D-SP problem uncovers a novel approach to the design of artificial, self-organizing emergent systems and possibly p
items.author: Jiří Kroc

items.title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
items.summary: Abstract Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are often difficult to predict and reproduce even when extrinsic sources of randomness are controlled, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here we propose riddled basin geometry as a unifying dynamical systems mechanism: every initialization leading to one solution lies arbitrarily close to initializations leading to different solutions, forming a fat fractal with structure at arbitrarily fine scales. Using a minimal neural network model, we analytically establish the classical route to riddling and derive a near-zero uncertainty exponent: even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability. In deep networks, intertwined training destinations and near-zero parameter-space exponents provide robust signatures consistent with riddling across the tested architectures, optimizers and training protocols, offering a common dynamical account of otherwise disparate empirical observations. We further introduce functional uncertainty exponents, extending these diagnostics of scale-insensitive irreproducibility from parameter space to the learned functions themselves. Together, our results support riddled basin geometry as a candidate organizing principle for irreproducibility in deep learning, with practical implications for optimization and the reliable deployment of artificial intelligence.
items.author: Andrew Ly, Pulin Gong

items.title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle
items.summary: Pioneering thermal transport measurements on two-dimensional electron gases in high magnetic fields have demonstrated that the quantized Hall state at filling factor ν = 5/2 has a thermal Hall conductance κ quantized in half-integer multiples of κ 0 = π 2 k B 2 T / 3 h . Half-integer κ / κ 0 is a signature of neutral Majorana edge modes, in turn linked to the presence of non-Abelian anyon excitations in the bulk. However, the experimentally observed value of κ corresponds to the “PH-Pfaffian” state, in tension with numerical studies which instead favor either the Pfaffian or the AntiPfaffian. A variety of mechanisms have been invoked to explain this discrepancy, but have been either ruled out by further experiments or else involve fine-tuning. Building on density-matrix-renormalization group studies of physically realistic edges and analytic calculations of edge structure, we propose an alternative resolution of this puzzle involving an “edge reconstruction” solely involving the neutral Majorana sector of the theory. Such a Majorana edge reconstruction can “screen” a Pfaffian or AntiPfaffian bulk, so that transport signatures become indistinguishable from those of the PH-Pfaffian. We argue that this physically natural scenario is consistent with experiment.
items.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
items.author: Tevž Lotrič, Taige Wang, Michael P. Zaletel, Steven H. Simon et al.

items.title: Scalable quantum state preparation via large-language-model-driven discovery
items.summary: Efficient quantum state preparation remains a central challenge in first-principles quantum simulations of dynamics in quantum field theories, where the Hilbert space is intrinsically infinite-dimensional. Here, we introduce a large language model (LLM)-assisted framework for quantum-circuit design that systematically scales state-preparation circuits to large lattice volumes. Applied to a 1+1d XY spin chain, the LLM autonomously discovers a compact 4-parameter circuit that captures boundary-induced symmetry breaking with sub-percent energy deviation, enabling successful validation on the \texttt{Zuchongzhi} quantum processor. Guided by this insight, we extend the framework to 2+1d quantum field theories, where scalable variational ansätze have remained elusive. For a scalar field theory, the search yields a symmetry-preserving, 3-parameter shallow-depth ansatz whose optimized parameters converge to size-independent constants for lattices $n \ge 4$, providing, to our knowledge, the first scalable ansatz for this class of 2+1d models. Our results establish a practical route toward AI-assisted, human-guided discovery in quantum simulation.
items.author: Qing-Hong Cao, Zong-Yue Hou, Yingying Li, Xiaohui Liu et al.

items.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
items.summary: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems. We prove that, under local energy relaxation and dephasing noise, MDD achieves the maximum entanglement fidelity attainable by any DD scheme based on bang-bang operations to first order in evolution time. On the IBM Eagle processor, MDD achieved up to a $450$-fold improvement in the success probability of a $14$-qubit quantum Fourier transform, and improved the accuracy of ground-state energy estimation for $N_2$ in the $56$-qubit sample-based quantum diagonalization compared with the standard XX-pulse DD. These results establish MDD as a scalable and effective approach for suppressing decoherence in large-scale quantum algorithms.
items.author: Jeongwoo Jae, Chang Won Lee, Juzar Thingna, Yeong-Dae Kwon et al.

items.title: Metalearning of Gibbs states for many-body Hamiltonians with applications to quantum Boltzmann machines
items.summary: The preparation of quantum Gibbs states is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, essential for applications ranging from modeling open quantum systems to quantum machine learning. Building on the Meta-Variational Quantum Eigensolver framework proposed by Cervera-Lierta et al. and a problem-driven ansatz design, we introduce two meta-learning algorithms: Meta-Variational Quantum Thermalizer (Meta-VQT) and Neural Network Meta-VQT (NN-Meta VQT) for efficient thermal state preparation of parametrized Hamiltonians on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. Meta-VQT utilizes a fully quantum ansatz, while NN Meta-VQT integrates a quantum--classical hybrid architecture. Both use collective optimization over a finite set of training parameter values to prepare approximate Gibbs states at held-out parameter values within the sampled parameter domain. We validate our methods on Transverse Field Ising Models (TFIM) with up to eight qubits and on a two-qubit Heisenberg model with all field terms. Within these finite-size benchmarks, the trained models accurately prepare thermal states at test points inside the training interval. For the six and eight qubit cases of TFIM, meta-learned parameters when combined with appropriately designed ansatz serve as warm-start initializations, significantly outperforming random initializations in the optimization tasks. Furthermore, a 3 qubit Kitaev ring example showcases our algorithm's effectiveness across finite-temperature crossover regimes. Finally, we apply our algorithms to train a Quantum Boltzmann Machine (QBM) on a 2-qubit Heisenberg model with all field terms, achieving enhanced training efficiency, improved Gibbs state accuracy, and a 30-fold runtime speedup over existing techniques such as variational quantum imaginar
items.author: Ruchira V Bhat, Rahul Bhowmick, Avinash Kumar Singh, Krishna Kumar Sabapathy

items.title: Fully quantum algorithmic framework for partial differential equation-constrained optimization
items.summary: Partial differential equation (PDE)-constrained optimization, where an optimization problem is subject to PDE constraints, arises in various applications such as design, control, and inference. Solving such problems is computationally demanding because it requires repeatedly solving a PDE and using its solution within an optimization process. In this paper, we first propose a fully coherent quantum algorithm for solving PDE-constrained optimization problems. The proposed method combines a quantum PDE solver that prepares the solution vector as a quantum state, and a quantum optimizer that assumes oracle access to a quantized objective function. The central idea is the explicit construction of the oracle in a form of block-encoding for the objective function, which coherently uses the output of a quantum PDE solver. This enables us to avoid classical access to the full solution that requires quantum state tomography canceling out the potential quantum speedups. We also derive the overall computational complexity of the proposed method with respect to parameters for optimization and PDE simulation, where quantum speedup is inherited from the underlying quantum PDE solver. We numerically demonstrate the validity of the proposed method by applications, including a parameter calibration problem in the Black-Scholes equation and a material parameter design problem in the wave equation. This work presents the concept of composing quantum subroutines so that the weakness of one (i.e., prohibitive readout overhead) is neutralized by the strength of another (i.e., coherent oracle access), toward a bottleneck-free quantum algorithm.
items.author: Yuki Sato, Jumpei Kato, Hiroshi Yano, Kosuke Ito et al.

items.title: Detector-optimized wavelength-hybrid entangled photon source for scalable fiber quantum key distribution
items.summary: Abstract Practical deployment of entanglement-based quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires photon sources that simultaneously address fiber transmission loss, detector performance, and system cost–constraints that are individually well-understood but collectively unresolved in current source designs. Here we present a detector-optimized, wavelength-hybrid entangled photon source (EPS) that resolves this trilemma by design and show its performance in a QKD system. The source uses type-0 spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a crossed-crystal periodically poled KTiOPO $$_4$$ (ppKTP) configuration pumped at 473 nm, generating polarization-entangled photon pairs at 680 nm and 1550 nm. This highly nondegenerate wavelength combination is engineered to route the 680 nm photon to a high-efficiency, low-cost Si-SPAD detector while transmitting the 1550 nm photon through standard telecom fiber with minimum attenuation. The source achieves a spectral brightness of (1.9 × 10 3 )s −1 mW −1 GHz −1 pairs over a 300 GHz phase-matching bandwidth, with polarization entanglement visibilities of (97.3 ± 1.0)% and (94.9 ± 1.6)% in the H/V and D/A bases, corresponding to a state fidelity of $$\ge $$ (96.1 ± 1.3)%. These results establish the wavelength-hybrid approach as a scalable and cost-effective building block for deployed entanglement-based QKD nodes and future quantum network infrastructure.
items.author: Vasile-Laurenţiu Dosan, Alek Lagarrigue, Alessandro Zannotti, Tushar Parab et al.

items.title: Altermagnetic materials library in intercalated transition-metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: Altermagnets represent a promising class of magnetic materials owing to their distinctive spin-split band structures in the absence of net magnetization. Here, we present a first-principles investigation of altermagnetism in magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with the general formula T$_y$MX$_2$ (T= 3$d$-transition metal, M= transition-metal, X=chalcogen, $y$= 1/3 or 1/4). For a TMD host with 2H structure, compounds exhibiting A-type antiferromagnetism are $g$-wave altermagnets by symmetry. We identify several intercalated TMDs fulfilling the conditions for altermagnetic order to be realized. Several of these candidate materials display spin-splittings at the Fermi level as large as 100 meV.
items.author: Ezra Day-Roberts, Huan Wu, Onur Erten, A. S Botana

items.title: Efficient absolute interface energy calculations for heterostructures: Synergy between localized basis sets, large vacuum, and surface passivation techniques
items.author: Sreejith Pallikkara Chandrasekharan, Sofia Apergi, Charles Cornet, Laurent Pédesseau

items.title: Solving the mysteries of quantum mechanics: why nature abhors a continuum
items.summary: Abstract Feynman asserted that interference is the only mystery in quantum mechanics (QM). It is concluded that the reason for this mystery, and thereby the related mysteries of complementarity, non-commutativity of observables, the uncertainty principle and violation of Bell's equality, is that the Hilbert space continuum of QM is unphysical. We describe a theory of quantum physics—rational QM (RaQM)—in which Hilbert space is (gravitationally) discretized. The key to solving the mysteries of QM in RaQM is a ubiquitous number-theoretic property of the cosine function, concealed in QM when angles range over the continuum. This property implies that the laws of physics are profoundly holistic, but not non-local. In the former, correlations between remote parts of the universe exist, but an intervention at one place cannot instantaneously influence affairs at the other. In the latter, such interventions can spread non-causally. Examples of holistic theories include Mach's principle, Penrose spin networks or the fractal geometry of chaotic attractors. Indeed, RaQM solves the deepest mystery of all; why nature makes use of complex numbers. It is to permit realistic incommensurate discretizations of incompatible observables. Such a solution is wholly concealed in the continuum theory of QM.
items.source: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
items.author: T. N. Palmer

items.title: Gigahertz-Clocked Generation of Highly Indistinguishable Photons at C-Band Wavelengths
items.summary: Abstract High-performance single-photon sources at telecom C-band wavelengths are key building blocks for applications in long-distance quantum communication. Here, we report the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. This is achieved by coherently driving the biexciton transition (T1XX=64(1) ps) of a semiconductor quantum dot embedded in a microcavity with strong asymmetric Purcell enhancement. Employing pulsed two-photon resonant excitation, strong multiphoton suppression with g(2)(0) 85% are observed. The observed photon indistinguishability is close to the theoretical limit expected for the photonically engineered radiative cascade and matches values obtained at lower repetition rates. Our results show a substantial advancement toward interference-based quantum information protocols at unprecedented data rates in the telecom C-band.
items.author: Robert Behrends, Lucas Rickert, Nils D. Kewitz, Martin von Helversen et al.

items.title: Mixed Thiolate/Alkoxide Antimony Cages for Reversed-Bilayer Vesicle Self-Assembly and Dye Protection in Organic Media
items.summary: A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Structural analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers, consistent with pnictogen-bonded vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.
