items.summary: Exact normalizable solutions of quantum constraints form a symplectic submanifold of the space of rays, whereas classical first-class constraints define a surface on which the symplectic form is degenerate. We ask how the degenerate directions can be recovered when quantum theory is regarded as fundamental and the constraints are imposed through a single positive master operator. For a nonnegative master function whose zero set is a Morse--Bott critical manifold, the image of the linearized Hamiltonian vector field is the symplectic orthogonal of the zero set, and coisotropy is equivalent to this linearization having square zero. The image is fixed by the zero set, but the theorem identifies it with the response of the master dynamics, which makes it accessible to quantum states. Three realizations follow. The exact quantum physical space is the opposite, rotational case of the same dichotomy. For quadratic masters, the bottom of the spectrum is $(\hbar/2)\Tr_+L$, so first-class zero sets carry no offset of order $\hbar$; within the harmonic approximation this explains the $\hbar$ versus $\hbar^2$ offsets observed in tests of the master-constraint programme. Finally, the second time derivative of the limiting covariance of a semiclassical packet, which can be determined by bounded probes, has the gauge distribution as its image. Two oscillators at fixed total energy give exact master evolution, an exact realization of this covariance shear, and the reduced symplectic limit. For the non-Abelian SL(2,$\R$) model we compute the coherent and Weyl master symbols, prove essential self-adjointness and a finite-time propagation estimate, and derive the spectral bottom $\hbar^2/2$.
items.author: Alejandro Corichi

items.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
items.summary: The "Rayleigh limit" is not an intrinsic property of light, but a consequence of sub-optimal measurement of collected photons by the imaging instrument. To overcome this limitation, we present Adaptive Information Mining, a framework that achieves super-resolution by using sequentially refined measurements for incoming photons. Our approach employs a reconfigurable imaging system that dynamically reshapes the instrument measurement responses to maximize the Fisher information and guide scene estimation toward the fundamental quantum limit, even in deep sub-Rayleigh regimes. We demonstrate that this approach achieves an estimation error 2-5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging when imaging point sources, without requiring any prior knowledge of their positions and brightnesses. Importantly, we demonstrate that AIM can be extended to fully blind multi-parameter estimation in scenarios involving an unknown number of sources or turbulence-induced wavefront distortions. Our approach addresses the limitations of conventional fixed imaging, offering a practical path toward quantum-limited super-resolution imaging.
items.author: Seungman Choi, Peter Menart, Andrew Schramka, Zubin Jacob

items.title: Homodyne Unravelling and Parameter Estimation in Squeezed Thermal Baths
items.summary: We derive an alternative formulation of the stochastic master equation describing the evolution of quantum systems continuously measured via homodyne detection in a squeezed-thermal environment. This formulation allows us to identify two distinct collapse operators, corresponding respectively to the monitored and unmonitored channels, and to express the quantum state evolution directly in terms of Kraus-like operators. As a consequence, it facilitates the application of advanced numerical methods that account for higher-order corrections and discrete-time monitoring, and it also enables the efficient numerical evaluation of Cramér-Rao bounds in parameter estimation problems. To demonstrate the latter, we evaluate the Fisher information of the continuous homodyne monitoring for qubit frequency estimation in the presence of a squeezed-thermal bath. Our results show that exponential scaling of the steady-state Fisher information rate with squeezing is retained even at non-zero temperature.
items.author: Eoin O'Connor, Francesco Albarelli, Marco G. Genoni

items.title: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes
items.summary: We construct a rank-one minimal informationally complete measurement (MIC) with an invertible dual operator and prove that, for arbitrary finite input and output dimensions, a channel universally preserves measurement incompatibility if and only if its input space contains a noiseless code subspace of the full output dimension. Preserving the compatibility threshold of a finite family of binary measurements already guarantees such a code. Furthermore, for every $d\ge2$, there exists a family of binary measurements that is incompatible on the full space but compatible after compression to any proper subspace. These results resolve the conjecture of Chitambar and Zhang and the existence question posed by Uola and coauthors. We also give an explicit construction of exact encodings and show that, for a sufficiently small shift in the compatibility threshold, the transmission error of an approximate encoding is bounded by a constant times the square of the shift. These results establish a connection between measurement compatibility, quantum steering, and quantum error correction.
items.author: Yu-Xuan Zhang, Jing-Ling Chen

items.title: Security Analysis of Ekert-type QKD Protocol Coming Under Cloning Attacks
items.summary: We analyze the security of an Ekert type bipartite key distribution protocol coming under cloning attacks by an untrusted observer. Precisely, an eavesdropper is assumed to intercept and apply an asymmetric, phase-variant cloner on one or both qubits which are transmitted over public channel from an authenticated source to the trusted parties. We partially characterize two-qubit states from the perspective of designing a QKD protocol that can generate a distillable secret key among the trusted users even under such cloning attacks. We rely upon Devetak Winter framework for computing key rate so as to identify states, which when used in the protocol, secret-key can be distilled. Utility of an entangled state, for designing a successful QKD protocol, changes from single-qubit to double-qubits cloning attacks. Interestingly, we can distinguish some useful families of two-qubit entangled states when only one of the transmitted qubits is cloned by a malicious third party.
items.author: Kaushiki Mukherjee, Sumana Karmakar

items.title: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage
items.summary: Every quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol must limit the information available outside the users' laboratories. In device-independent QKD this is essentially the only assumption made on the devices. In a prepare-and-measure setting it cannot be imposed strictly, since the sender's device must emit a signal that depends on her private input. The natural replacement, and a minimal one, is a leakage bound: a bound on how much information about the input leaves the sender's laboratory, through the intended signal or through any side channel. We ask how far this unavoidable requirement can replace a detailed model of the source. We show that this single bound, quantified by the probability of guessing the input from everything the source emits, suffices to prove security against collective attacks. In our analysis, nothing is assumed about the precise form of the emitted states, their dimension, energy or purity, nor about the receiver's measurement device, beyond the standard requirement that it does not leak Bob's data. The standard B92 and BB84 protocols do not certify any key under this minimal leakage bound assumption. But closely related protocols can and, in the ideal limit, achieve one secret bit per key round. For noisy implementations, we compute key rates using semidefinite programming relaxations. Our best protocols tolerate visibilities down to 0.84, corresponding to an 8% quantum bit error rate, compared with the 11% threshold of standard device-dependent BB84.
items.author: Abhishek Mishra, Michele Masini, Maria Balanzó-Juandó, Armin Tavakoli et al.

items.title: Noncontextuality inequalities for prepare-transform-measure scenarios
items.summary: We provide the first systematic technique for deriving witnesses of contextuality in prepare-transform-measure scenarios. More specifically, we show how linear quantifier elimination can be used to compute a polytope of correlations consistent with generalized noncontextuality in such scenarios. This polytope is specified as a set of noncontextuality inequalities that are necessary and sufficient conditions for observed data in the scenario to admit of a classical explanation relative to any linear operational identities, if one ignores some constraints from diagram preservation. While including these latter constraints generally leads to tighter inequalities, it seems that nonlinear quantifier elimination would be required to systematically include them. We also provide a linear program which can certify the nonclassicality of a set of numerical data arising in a prepare-transform-measure experiment. We apply our results to get a robust noncontextuality inequality for transformations that can be violated within the stabilizer subtheory. Finally, we give a simple algorithm for computing all the linear operational identities holding among a given set of states, of transformations, or of measurements.
items.author: David Schmid, Roberto D. Baldijão, John H. Selby, Ana Belén Sainz et al.

items.title: A General Framework for Gradient-Based Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Circuits using Qubit Discovery as a Case Study
items.summary: Engineering the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is fundamental to the design of quantum systems. Automating Hamiltonian design through gradient-based optimization can dramatically accelerate this process. However, computing the gradients of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hamiltonian–a large, sparse matrix–relative to system properties poses a significant challenge, especially for arbitrary systems. Superconducting quantum circuits offer substantial flexibility in Hamiltonian design, making them an ideal platform for this task. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for the gradient-based optimization of superconducting quantum circuits, leveraging the SQcircuit software package. By addressing the challenge of calculating the gradient of the eigensystem for large, sparse Hamiltonians and integrating automatic differentiation within SQcircuit, our framework enables efficient and precise computation of gradients for various circuit properties or custom-defined metrics, streamlining the optimization process. We apply this framework to the qubit discovery problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying qubit designs with superior performance metrics. The optimized circuits show improvements in a heuristic measure of gate count, upper bounds on gate speed, decoherence time, and resilience to noise and fabrication errors compared to existing qubits. While this methodology is showcased through qubit optimization and discovery, it is versatile and can be extended to tackle other optimization challenges in superconducting quantum hardware design.
items.author: Taha Rajabzadeh, Alex Boulton-McKeehan, Sam Bonkowsky, David I. Schuster et al.

items.title: Valley Hall viscosity in gapped graphene with and without a magnetic field
items.summary: Hall viscosity is conventionally defined through the stress response to time-dependent strain, a perturbation that is difficult to implement in solid-state experiments. We formulate a related viscoelastic response to static, spatially inhomogeneous electric fields and compare it with the strain-based response. For gapped graphene in a perpendicular magnetic field, the two formulations give the same Landau-level response, whose Hall viscosity is asymmetric between the two valleys. At zero magnetic field, a valley-even quantum-metric coefficient combines with the valley-odd Hall conductivity to produce equal and opposite valley-resolved responses; global time-reversal symmetry therefore forces the net Hall viscosity to vanish. In an insulating state, exact particle--hole symmetry eliminates this zero-field response, whereas particle--hole-symmetry breaking generates a cutoff-dependent geometric contribution from the occupied Fermi sea. These results connect valley-dependent viscoelasticity with electromagnetic response in gapped Dirac materials and clarify the conditions under which a valley Hall viscosity can arise.
items.author: Danyu Shu, Hiroshi Funaki, Ai Yamakage, Ryotaro Sano et al.

items.title: Numerical Computation of the Density of States of Aperiodic Multiscale Schrödinger Operators
items.summary: Abstract. Computing the electronic structure of incommensurate materials is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, requiring efficient ways to approximate spectral quantities such as the density of states (DoS). In this paper, we numerically investigate two distinct approaches for approximating the DoS of incommensurate Hamiltonians for small values of the incommensurability parameters [Formula: see text] (e.g., small twist angle, or small lattice mismatch): the first employs a momentum-space decomposition, and the second exploits a semiclassical expansion with respect to [Formula: see text]. In particular, we compare these two methods using a one-dimensional toy model. We check their consistency by comparing the asymptotic expansion terms of the DoS, and it is shown that, for full DoS, the two methods exhibit good agreement in the small [Formula: see text] limit, while discrepancies arise for less small [Formula: see text], which indicates the importance of higher-order corrections in the semiclassical method for such regimes. We find these discrepancies to be caused by oscillations in the DoS at the semiclassical analogues of Van Hove singularities, which can be explained qualitatively, and quantitatively for [Formula: see text] small enough, by a semiclassical approach. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://zenodo.org/records/20214148 and in the supplementary materials ( DOS_multiscale_supplementary_material.pdf [270KB], DOS_multiscale_supporting
items.author: Eric Cancès B, Daniel Massatt, Long Meng, Étienne Polack et al.

items.title: Analysis of LIGO glitches using t-SNE during the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
items.summary: This paper presents an analysis of noise transients observed in LIGO data during the first part of the fourth observing run, using the unsupervised machine learning technique t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) to examine the behavior of glitch groups. Based on the t-SNE output, we apply Agglomerative Clustering in combination with the Silhouette Score to determine the optimal number of groups. We then track these groups over time and investigate correlations between their occurrence and environmental or instrumental conditions. At the Livingston observatory, the most common glitches during O4a were seasonal and associated with ground motion, whereas at Hanford, the most prevalent glitches were related to instrumental conditions.
items.author: T. A. Ferreira, Gabriela González, Osvaldo Salas

items.title: Fabry-Pérot interferometry with stochastic anyonic sources
items.summary: We investigate the interference of Laughlin quasiparticles (QPs) in the fractional quantum Hall regime that are stochastically injected into a Fabry--Pérot interferometer. We find that the effective Aharonov--Bohm (AB) phase accumulated along the interferometer loop acquires an additional contribution of $\sin(2πλ)/2$ per QP present on it, where $πλ$ is the QP exchange phase. This contribution originates from time-domain braiding processes associated with injected QPs passing the interferometer quantum point contacts. In the limit of symmetric QP injection, the tunneling current noise exhibits AB oscillations as a function of the total injected current, providing access to the exchange phase $πλ$. In the regime of large total injection, we identify a universal Fano factor that displays power-law scaling and a characteristic phase shift reflecting time-domain QP braiding at the interferometer QPCs. These results are relevant for accessing anyonic exchange statistics in mesoscopic interferometers.
items.author: Sarthak Girdhar, Edvin G. Idrisov, Thomas L. Schmidt

items.title: Fault-tolerant simulation of the electronic structure using projector augmented-waves and Bloch orbitals
items.summary: Strongly correlated materials are a natural target for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but they require tools beyond those developed for molecules. Electronic wavefunctions vary rapidly near nuclei yet remain delocalized across many unit cells, and bulk properties must be converged systematically with respect to finite-size errors. To resolve such issues, we present the Bloch--UPAW framework that combines Bloch-orbital $k$-space structure with unitary projector-augmented-wave (UPAW) augmentation. The UPAW Hamiltonian, expressed directly in the Bloch basis, retains explicit control of Brillouin-zone sampling, and incorporates near-nuclear physics through strictly local on-site corrections. The construction is independent of the underlying one-particle representation, so it applies to both plane-wave and localized bases, and it handles supercells for symmetry-breaking phenomena more efficiently. We derive a linear-combination-of-unitaries decomposition and a block-encoding circuit suitable for qubitization; UPAW augmentation adds one ancilla qubit and no Toffoli gates at leading order relative to a Bloch-only block encoding. Asymptotically, the Toffoli cost scales as $\mathcal{O}(N_k^3)$ when refining the $k$-mesh and as $\mathcal{O}(N_a^{3.5})$ when enlarging the supercell, enabling convergence to be steered by the most favorable route for a given material. Resource estimates for bulk diamond show approximately an order-of-magnitude reduction in Toffoli count relative to prior work on periodic solids.
items.author: Rishabh Bhardwaj, Alexander Reed Muñoz, Travis E. Jones, John Golden

items.title: Low-rank geometry of two-qubit gates
items.summary: We present a framework based on the determinantal geometry of two-qubit gates. Combining the Weyl chamber representation with operator Schmidt theory, we interpret gate synthesis as a distance problem to determinantal varieties. This gives an operational geometry to the Weyl chamber, quantifying nonlocal complexity. We show that the square root iSWAP gate is the closest perfect entangler to the variety of local operations, and that no perfect entangler can be approximated by a local gate with average gate fidelity above 79.8%. The three different determinantal costs form a synthesis-adapted coordinate system that encodes nonlocal complexity and generally reconstructs the Weyl chamber.
items.author: Llorenç Balada Gaggioli

items.title: Non-Hermitian Rayleigh-Schrödinger-like perturbation theory at exceptional point
items.summary: Abstract We develop a Rayleigh-Schrödinger-like perturbation theory for non-Hermitian quantum systems at an exceptional point of order N. Working in the Jordan basis of the unperturbed Hamiltonian and employing a Puiseux expansion of the perturbed eigenvalues and eigenstates, we derive explicit recursion relations for the expansion coefficients. The corrections to the unperturbed eigenvalue in the Puiseux expansion govern the splitting near the exceptional point; the first two are obtained iteratively in two equivalent forms. One is given in terms of the perturbation Hamiltonian in the Jordan basis, and the other in terms of the generator that drives the eigenvalue evolution with respect to the perturbation. The latter constitutes the exceptional-point counterpart of a geometric perturbation method recently developed for the non-exceptional-point regime. Both representations are verified explicitly for the N = 2 and N = 3 cases. We then apply the theory to an order-3 exceptional point realized in a dissipative three-level trapped-ion system.
items.author: Wei-Ming Chen, Chia-Yi Ju

items.title: TinyRoute: secure adaptive routing for intelligent transportation system using TinyML and few shot learning
items.summary: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) needs secure and adaptive communication mechanisms for addressing the dynamic vehicular mobility, routing instability, and increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks in Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V), Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I), and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) environments in which the recent VANET routing and intrusion detection approaches have improved routing efficiency or attack detection individually. However, it generally lack an integrated framework capable of simultaneously supporting adaptive routing, lightweight edge intelligence, and reliable zero-day attack detection under highly dynamic traffic conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes TinyRoute, a secure adaptive routing framework that integrates Geometric Deep Reinforcement Learning (Geo-DRL), Honey Badger Optimization (HBO), TinyML, and a CNN LSTM-based Few-Shot Learning Intrusion Detection System (FSL-IDS) in which the Geo-DRL performs mobility-aware route selection but HBO refines routing paths by avoiding malicious and congested regions. The lightweight on-device anomaly inference within autonomous vehicles is enabled by TinyML. With only the limited samples, the cloud based FSL-IDS detects both known and zero-day attacks respectively. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that TinyRoute achieves a routing latency of 28.4 ms, a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 96.7%, an intrusion detection accuracy of 95.2%, and a communication overhead of only 12.4 KB/s, outperforming recent state-of-the-art VANET routing and IDS approaches. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for secure, adaptive, and low-latency ITS communication.
items.author: S. Jagadeesan, A. Suresh, T. Vetriselvi, D. Tamil Priya et al.

items.title: Proof of hiding conjecture in Gaussian boson sampling
items.summary: Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) is a promising protocol for demonstrating quantum computational advantage. One of the key steps in the argument for classical hardness of GBS is the so-called “hiding conjecture'', which asserts that one can “hide'' a complex Gaussian matrix as a submatrix of the symmetric product of Haar unitary submatrices in total variation distance. In this paper, we prove the hiding conjecture for input states with all input modes squeezed, which is a setup that has recently been realized experimentally \cite{madsen2022}. In this setting, the hiding conjecture states that a o ( M ) × o ( M ) submatrix of an M × M circular orthogonal ensemble (COE) random matrix can be well-approximated by a complex symmetric Gaussian matrix in total variation distance as M → ∞ . This is the first rigorous proof of the hiding property for GBS in the experimentally relevant regime, and puts the argument for hardness of classically simulating GBS with the maximum number of squeezed input modes on a comparable level to that of the conventional boson sampling of [Aaronson and Arkhipov, Theory Comput. 9, 143 (2013)] \cite{aa}.
items.author: Laura Shou, Sarah H. Miller, Victor M. Galitski

items.title: Inductorless fast phase logic: Enabling two-order-of-magnitude density scaling for superconductor VLSI
items.summary: Abstract Fast phase logic (FPL) is a novel digital superconductor electronic (SCE) logic family that employs multiple junction types, including switching 0-Josephson junctions (0-JJs), non-switching 0-JJ stacks, and π-JJs. FPL enables flexible, automatable cell layouts, faster pulse propagation, reduced bias current via phaseshifting π-JJs, and minimized inductive loops, thereby reducing susceptibility to trapped flux and crosstalk.A fabrication process to support FPL is proposed. NbTiN superconductors offer small grain sizes, smooth surfaces, and thermal stability up to 400 ○ C, while high-Jc, self-shunted JJs enable compact devices. AlN dielectrics provide good crystal matching to NbTiN, improving superconducting properties. Projections indicate that FPL, combined with the proposed process, can achieve a two-order-of-magnitude increase in integration density over conventional RSFQ logic and a five-fold reduction in supply current. The increased density reduces latency and improves computational throughput, while NbTiN-based devices provide higher output voltage and impedance, improving compatibility with CMOS circuits. Further fabrication advancements, such as higher-Jc NbTiN-based JJs, higher processing temperatures, and stacked JJ structures, could enhance FPL implementation and scalability toward very large-scale integration (VLSI). FPL has the potential to significantly advance SCE technology, with near-term applications in accelerator cores for signal processing and artificial intelligence, and long-term potential in supercomputing. Its advantages are evaluated through an architectural study of a fast Fourier transform (FFT) circuit, with comparisons to CMOS and SFQ technologies for digital electronics.
items.author: Sasan Razmkhah, Massoud Pedram, Douglas Holmes

items.title: Instability as a quantum resource
items.summary: We consolidate coherence, athermality, and nonuniformity as sub-resources within an underlying quantum resource theory: instability. We formulate instability axiomatically as the transient information within a decaying physical system. Specifying a decay mechanism (e.g., dephasing, thermalization) recovers these familiar resources as specific manifestations of instability. We compute the one-shot distillation yield and dilution cost in various operational paradigms, and use them to pin down the extremal additive monotones. In the asymptotic regime, we show that all conversion rates are governed by a single additive monotone, and thereby establish a universal second law for instability.

items.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
items.summary: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.
items.author: Li Gao, Lijun Wang

items.title: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
items.summary: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states. A source of three entangled qubits is richer, since its nonlocality can be tested by the Mermin or the more demanding Svetlichny inequality. We ask how network nonlocality relates to these two single-source notions and find that the answer depends on the wiring. When two central nodes without inputs share every source, Bell-state measurements turn every Svetlichny violation into a network violation, and even all entangled generalised Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states violate the network inequality. When a single central node is shared, the relation reverses, and a network violation requires a Mermin violation of the source. With more sources, the maximal violation depends on whether their number is even or odd, and we give tight bounds for both cases. These results show that the way multipartite sources are wired decides which kind of nonlocality a network inherits.
items.author: Sudip Chakrabarty, Amit Kundu

items.title: Interference-induced dynamical crossovers in quantum walks on disordered square lattices
items.summary: We study discrete-time quantum walks with Fourier, Grover, and Hadamard coin operators on disordered square lattices, alongside classical random walks. Edges in the lattice are absent with a probability, $p$. In this case, both classical and quantum walks exhibit an essentially identical degradation of transport. We then study a general version of this model, in which the existing edges are retained. However, the absent edges are no longer absent, but now become partially transmitting, with a transmission coefficient $f$. We find that the response is now quite sensitive to the walk protocol and coin symmetry. The classical walk exhibits asymptotic stability of the anomalous diffusion exponent, $β(t)$. In comparison, quantum walks exhibit a monotonically decaying $β(t)$ beyond the initial transient regime, leading to the absence of quantum diffusion in two dimensions. We map the transport regimes in the $(f,p)$ plane and identify the contour for $β=1$, which separates the subdiffusive and superdiffusive regimes. We also examine the effective diffusion coefficient, the inverse participation ratio, and the first two moments of edge transmission. We restrict ourselves to analyzing bulk propagation prior to finite-size boundary reflections. The results indicate that quantum transport depends significantly on coin-specific interference and cannot be fully described by transmission statistics alone.
items.author: Ramnarayan Bera, Arijit Roy, Soumyadip Ghosh, Soumen Roy

items.title: Sparse Carleman Embeddings for Nonlinear Discrete Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Discrete nonlinear dynamical systems arise in population models, iterative optimization, and numerical simulations, where computing many iterations can be costly in high dimensions. We study Carleman embedding for forced quadratic discrete systems and its application to quantum state preparation. Under explicit stability and initial-state assumptions, we prove that the truncation error decreases geometrically with the embedding degree, uniformly over all iterations. A central obstacle in discrete time is that the lifted update can become dense even when the original coefficient maps are sparse. We overcome this obstacle by constructing an exact auxiliary linear-system representation that applies the coefficient maps one tensor factor at a time, with row and column sparsities bounded independently of the truncation degree. After rescaling, the associated history system has a condition number that grows linearly with the iteration count, uniformly in the truncation degree. These results yield a quantum algorithm for preparing an approximation to the normalized $n$th iterate with constant success probability. Under coherent input-access assumptions, and for fixed sparsity, stability parameters, and a known positive lower bound on the final-state norm, the oracle query complexity is linear in $n$ and polylogarithmic in the inverse accuracy. Numerical experiments in one and three dimensions illustrate the convergence of the truncated embedding.
items.author: Hsuan-Cheng Wu, Xiantao Li

items.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
items.summary: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. Th
items.author: M. E. Shirokov

items.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
items.summary: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.
items.author: Zhi-Yao Ning, Zi-Xiang Li, Naoki Kawashima

items.title: Growth Phase Map of α and \b{eta} Tantalum as a Function of Growth Temperature and Oxygen Partial Pressure
items.summary: Tantalum thin films are used in low-loss superconducting quantum circuits, yet the growth conditions governing selection of $α$-Ta(110), $α$-Ta(111), and metastable $β$-Ta on c-plane sapphire remain uncertain. We deposited 100 nm Ta films by dc magnetron sputtering on Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) at 300-900 $^\circ$C while varying the O$_2$ partial pressure from a $5.5\times10^{-11}$ Torr ultrahigh-vacuum baseline to $2.23\times10^{-4}$ Torr. Absorption-corrected X-ray diffraction texture coefficients were used to construct a ternary phase-orientation growth map in terms of temperature and the oxygen-to-Ta impingement flux ratio ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}\leq4.8\times10^{-6}$ to 19). Without added oxygen, $α$-Ta(110) dominated at every temperature. At an O$_2$ pressure of only $2.5\times10^{-9}$ Torr ($2Φ_{O_2}/Φ_{Ta}=2.2\times10^{-4}$), $α$-Ta(111) accounted for 98-99% of the normalized texture weight from 300 to 700 $^\circ$C, decreasing to 65% at 900 $^\circ$C. Substantial $β$-Ta formed only at the highest oxygen dose, dominating at 300 $^\circ$C and disappearing at 900 $^\circ$C. The apparent $β$(001)/$α$(110) selection energy of $1.07\pm0.16$ eV is comparable to the activation energy for oxygen diffusion in Ta, consistent with oxygen transport influencing phase selection. Oxygen also produced orientation-dependent changes in crystallite size and microstrain. These findings establish oxygen-controlled processing windows for phase- and orientation-selective growth of Ta films for superconducting devices.
items.author: Marius O. Eji, Tyler J. Kirkpatrick, Ty J. Cawein, Joseph P. Corbett

items.title: Compositional Operational Rank, Smooth Realizability, and Dimensional Reduction
items.summary: Higher-dimensional theories distinguish the dimensionality of a microscopic description from the number of directions accessible to a physical observer. Relating these notions requires not only dimensional reduction, but also a consistent preservation of operational independence across different levels of description. We establish sufficient conditions under which a compositional operational rank is preserved first as the dimension of a smooth integral leaf and then as an observable Fisher-information rank. The key requirement is closure-faithfulness: the smooth realization must preserve the dependency relations of the operational closure, rather than merely its total rank. Together with real representability, constant rank, involutivity, and observer/scale compatibility, this yields a local integral leaf whose dimension equals the operational rank. A further primary-identification condition is required at the measurement level. If an independently specified observer image coincides locally with the primary integral distribution and the admissible protocols provide local resolution, finite labeled-mixture closure, and locally constant outcome support, then the same rank can be realized by a finite composite Fisher-information protocol. The construction holds for arbitrary finite rank. At r = 4 it provides a conditional operational criterion for dimensional reduction in higher-dimensional theories: a viable reduction must preserve the relevant operational dependency structure, not merely produce four effective coordinates. Quantum-hardware negative controls further show that the same restricted Fisher rank can conceal different larger ranks under a broader pre-specified measurement protocol. The framework therefore constrains the operational outcome of dimensional reduct
items.author: Nikolay D. Tulupov, Alexander M. Tishin

items.title: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
items.summary: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.
items.author: Massimiliano F. Sacchi

items.title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
items.summary: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal. Furthermore, LSD-$0$ operates on a sparsified decoding graph of a fraction of the size of the full detector error model, which simplifies the resources required by specialized hardware to support it. Overall, the DAWG+LSD-$0$ decoder represents a viable low-cost BP-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes.
items.author: Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Francisco Garcia-Herrero, Ruben M. Otxoa, Reza Dastbasteh

items.title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
items.summary: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.
items.author: Mustapha Tarboun, Mohamed Amazioug

items.title: Distillable entanglement is continuous
items.summary: We prove continuity of distillable entanglement, the optimal asymptotic rate at which copies of a bipartite state can be converted into maximally entangled pairs by local operations and classical communication (LOCC) with vanishing error. We establish an explicit asymptotic continuity bound that holds for arbitrary bipartite states and depends logarithmically on the system dimension. This bound has the same structure as known continuity bounds for conditional entropy, entanglement cost, and relative entropy of entanglement. Our proof constructs an explicit LOCC protocol that converts either of two arbitrary bipartite states into the other at an ebit cost that vanishes as their trace distance tends to zero.
items.author: Lukas Schmitt, David Sutter

items.title: Nonlinear coupling between motional modes in trapped-ion quantum processors
items.summary: Trapped-ion crystals are a leading platform for quantum information science, but achieving the high-fidelity entangling gates required for fault-tolerant quantum computing becomes harder as system size increases. As systems scale, spectral crowding makes low-order nonlinear resonances between collective motional modes increasingly common and can limit gate performance, especially in monolithic or global-mode architectures. We develop a general model to identify and simulate nonlinear motional-mode coupling (NoMoCou) arising from third-order Coulomb terms and quantify its impact on the Molmer-Sorensen gate across linear chains and 2D crystals in rf and Penning traps. We delineate the regimes where NoMoCou dominates the error budget and provide design rules: detune operating points from low-order resonances, tune trap anisotropy to reshape spectra, and shape gate waveforms.
items.author: Wes Johnson, Brandon Ruzic

items.title: Early-time dynamics of heavy-ion collisions through energy correlators: Celestial blocks and the spacetime structure of out-of-equilibrium QCD matter
items.summary: Ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions provide a unique window into far-from-equilibrium states of QCD matter. The initial stages of these events are characterized by highly anisotropic, nonthermal dynamics that precede hydrodynamization, yet they remain largely inaccessible through conventional soft observables. In this work, we show that the substructure of mid-rapidity jets provides direct sensitivity to the spacetime structure of this early, anisotropic phase. Using classical Yang-Mills simulations and effective kinetic theory to model the early-time evolution of the jet quenching parameter, we compute the azimuthally differential energy-energy correlator within the BDMPS-Z framework. By decomposing the result into celestial blocks, we isolate the coefficients that encode the anisotropic geometry and dynamics of the underlying medium. We identify an observable that couples directly to spatial anisotropies in the out-of-equilibrium QCD matter and also discuss the impact of medium response on its behavior. We further extend our study to mid-rapidity jets generated with the JEWEL Monte-Carlo, adjusted to incorporate an anisotropic medium background, and find qualitative agreement with the analytical expectations. Finally, we discuss how higher-point energy correlators and generalized energy-flow operators can enhance the sensitivity to the microscopic structure of far-from-equilibrium QCD matter.
items.author: João Barata, José Guilherme Milhano, Andrey V. Sadofyev, João M. Silva

items.title: Bell and EPR experiments with signalling data
items.summary: Abstract The no-signalling principle is a fundamental assumption in Bell-inequality and quantum-steering experiments. Nonetheless, experimental imperfections can lead to apparent violations beyond those expected from finite-sample statistics. Here, we propose extensions of local hidden variable and local hidden state theories that allow for bounded, operationally quantifiable, amounts of signalling. We show how non-classicality tests can be developed for these models, both through exact methods based on the full set of observed statistics and through corrections to the standard Bell and steering inequalities. We demonstrate the applicability of these methods via two scenarios that feature apparent signalling: an IBM quantum processor and post-selected data from inefficient detectors.
items.author: Lucas Maquedano, Sophie Egelhaaf, Amro Abou-Hachem, Jef Pauwels et al.

items.title: Classical simulability from operator entanglement scaling
items.summary: Local-operator entanglement (LOE) quantifies the nonlocal structure of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of many-body chaos. We provide rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be well-approximated by a matrix-product operator (MPO), given asymptotic scaling of its LOE $α$-Rényi entropies. Specifically, we prove that a volume law scaling for $α\geq 1$ implies that the operator cannot be approximated efficiently as an MPO while faithfully reproducing all expectation values. On the other hand, if we restrict to correlations over a relevant sub-class of (ensembles of) states, then logarithmic scaling of the $α< 1$ entropies implies MPO simulability. This result covers a range of relevant quantities, including infinite temperature autocorrelation functions, out-of-time-ordered correlators, and average-case expectation values over ensembles of computational basis states. Beyond this regime, we provide numerical evidence together with a random matrix model to argue that this simulability result also typically holds for arbitrary states. Our results put on firm footing the heuristic expectation that a low operator entanglement implies efficient tensor network representability, extending celebrated foundational results from the theory of matrix-product states and providing a formal link between quantum chaos and classical simulability.
items.author: Neil Dowling

items.title: Quantum protocols for time synchronisation and distribution: a critical assessment
items.summary: Precise time synchronisation underpins critical infrastructure from telecommunications and financial markets to power grids and scientific metrology. Several families of quantum protocols have been proposed and demonstrated for clock synchronisation and time distribution, exploiting entangled photon pairs, quantum key distribution (QKD) correlations, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and entangled clock networks. We critically assess these approaches, reviewing the main quantum time synchronisation (QTS) protocol families, quantifying the gap between theory and experiment, and identifying practical bottlenecks in sources, detectors, and channels. We survey the classical timing landscape from Network Time Protocol (NTP) and GPS to laboratory-grade optical frequency transfer, and compare quantum and classical methods at equivalent maturity. We examine use cases including financial trading, power grids, telecommunications, scientific metrology, and military applications, evaluating whether quantum timing offers a realistic advantage. We show that time transfer, not clock performance, is now the bottleneck for distributed optical timekeeping: the best demonstrated quantum synchronisation uncertainty (2.46 ps, over 20 km of fibre) falls two to three orders of magnitude short of what optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainties of 10 −18 –10 −19 require. The best deployed link, ELSTAB, calibrates to a few tens of picoseconds in the laboratory and to about 0.2 ns on its 421 km field installation, a further factor of twenty to a hundred behind, while research-grade classical links using optical frequency combs already reach the regime the clocks require, though none is in operational service. Our assessment is that quantum time synchronisation will not replace classical me
items.author: M. Krelina, Utku Tefek, Zeki Can Seskir, Kadir Durak

items.title: Zak-OTFS: A Predictable Physical Layer for Communications and Sensing
items.summary: This tutorial derives the mathematical foundations of what it means for a carrier waveform to be predictable and non-selective. We focus on Zak-OTFS, where each carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, formally a quasi-periodic localized function with specific periods along delay and Doppler. Viewed in the time domain, the Zak-OTFS carrier is realized as a pulse train modulated by a tone (termed a pulsone). We start by providing physical intuition, describing what it means for the Zak-OTFS carrier waveforms to be geometric modes of the Heisenberg-Weyl (HW) group of discrete delay and Doppler shifts that define the discrete-time communication model. In fact, we show that these geometric modes are common eigenvectors of a maximal commutative subgroup of our discrete HW group. When the channel delay spread is less than the delay period, and the channel Doppler spread is less than the Doppler period, we show that the Zak-OTFS input-output (I/O) relation is predictable and non-selective. Given the I/O response at one DD point in a frame, it is possible to predict the I/O response at all other points, without recourse to some mathematical model of the channel. While it may be intuitive that geometric modes of the HW group are predictable and non-selective wireless carriers, this is not a requirement. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition that depends on the ambiguity properties of the basis of carrier waveforms. In fact, we show that the structure of a pulse train modulated by a Hadamard matrix is common to several families of waveforms proposed for 6G, including Zak-OTFS, AFDM, OTSM and ODDM.
items.author: Sandesh Rao Mattu, Nishant Mehrotra, Venkatesh Khammammetti, Robert Calderbank

items.title: Noise spectroscopy of insulating and itinerant altermagnets
items.summary: One of the central goals in the emergent field of altermagnetism is the unambiguous experimental identification and characterization of altermagnetic order across a variety of compounds. This motivates exploring tools that can clearly distinguish altermagnets from antiferromagnets, based on symmetry signatures, and offer access to the dominant orbital character (e.g., $d$-wave vs. $g$-wave) of the magnetic order parameter. In this work, we theoretically explore the potential of noise magnetometry for this task, studying contributions from both magnons and itinerant electrons in different regimes and scenarios. While altermagnetism and antiferromagnetism also lead to different noise spectra for magnons, we find the most striking and symmetry-sensitive signatures in the charge fluctuations of itinerant altermagnets. Both for the homogeneous bulk case and in the presence of strain and/or around domain walls, we identify noise contributions that are only permitted by symmetry in the altermagnet and, thus, provide a unique signature of altermagnetism. Furthermore, the angular dependence of noise around domain walls also offers access to the orbital character of the altermagnet. On a more technical note, we discuss the role and relevance of lattice effects related to the dipole tensor. We hope that our work will help pave the way towards the clear experimental identification of altermagnetism across a wide range of candidate materials.
items.author: Lucas V. Pupim, Mathias S. Scheurer

items.title: Cosmo-SPINN: Fuzzy Dark Matter Simulations with Physics-informed Generative Networks
items.summary: Abstract Generative machine learning models have recently emerged as powerful tools for producing cosmological simulations. However, many existing emulators do not explicitly enforce the underlying physical dynamics governing cosmological evolution, often leading to artifacts and poor adherence to the evolution equations. In this work, we present a physics-informed generative U-Net framework for fuzzy dark matter (FDM) that addresses two complementary tasks: (i) the evolution of cosmological fields from initial conditions across a specified range of cosmological scale factors, and (ii) the super-resolution of FDM simulations at a specified cosmological scale factor. Our model incorporates a physics-informed loss function that explicitly enforces consistency with the underlying Schrödinger–Poisson (SP) dynamics during training. For the evolution task, we find that the inclusion of this physics-based loss significantly improves the quality of the predicted simulations, even when only a small amount of training data is available. Using 20% of the snapshots randomly sampled across the evolution interval, the model accurately interpolates the evolution between the sampled training snapshots in a 1 h −1 Mpc box. Furthermore, the framework generalizes effectively across previously unseen realizations of the initial conditions. For the super-resolution task, we present, for the first time, a generative super-resolution model trained on FDM simulations obtained by solving the full SP equations, considering both single and multiple realizations of the initial conditions and analyzing the role of the physics-informed loss in each case. Our approach enables modern generative modeling of cosmological simulations while maintaining physical consistency and substantially reducing gener
items.author: Ashutosh Kumar Mishra, Emma Elizabeth Tolley, Nicolas Cerardi

items.title: The imaginary component of the weak momentum: Spectral vanishing and gauge invariance
items.summary: Abstract We establish a rigorous functional-analytic framework for the imaginary component p I of the complex weak momentum p Q = p R + ip I , defined as the imaginary part of the local momentum field ℏ i ∇ ln ψ. For all wavefunctions in the Sobolev space H 1 (Ω), including those with nodal sets, we prove that the expectation value of p I vanishes identically -a structural consequence of the regularity of the probability density ρ = |ψ| 2 rather than a dynamical coincidence -so that the imaginary component carries no contribution to the physical momentum expectation value. The derivation makes no appeal to the polar form ψ = Re iS/ℏ and holds for any ψ ∈ H 1 (Ω). We further prove four structural results: (i) the quantum potential of Bohm arises entirely from p I , and its expectation value satisfies the exact identity ⟨V qu ⟩ = ⟨p 2 I ⟩/2m, proved via Sobolev integration by parts without invoking the polar form -from which the known Fisher information relation ⟨V qu ⟩ = ℏ 2 I[ρ]/8m [1, 2] follows as a corollary; (ii) the group velocity of a Bloch band is the density-weighted average of the local transport velocity p R /m with no contribution from p I ; (iii) the decomposition is gauge-invariant under magnetic minimal coupling, with the vector potential acting exclusively on the real component p R ; and (iv) the result extends to curved Riemannian manifolds, establishing the decomposition as an intrinsic property of the wavefunction independent of any particular representation. Together, these results provide a rigorous operator-theoretic framework for the imaginary weak momentum, while preserving the spectral integrity of linear quantum theory.

items.title: Real-time detection of correlated quasiparticle tunneling events in a multi-qubit superconducting device
items.summary: Quasiparticle tunneling events are a source of decoherence and correlated errors in superconducting circuits. Understanding and ultimately mitigating these errors calls for real-time detection of quasiparticle tunneling events on individual devices. In this work, we simultaneously detect quasiparticle tunneling events in two co-housed, charge-sensitive transmons coupled to a common waveguide. We measure background quasiparticle tunneling rates at the single-hertz level, with temporal resolution of tens of microseconds. Using time-tagged coincidence analysis, we show that individual events are uncorrelated across devices, whereas burst episodes occur about once per minute and are largely correlated. These bursts have a characteristic lifetime of 7 ms and induce a thousand-fold increase in the quasiparticle tunneling rate across both devices. In addition, we identify a rarer subset of bursts which are accompanied by a shift in the offset charge, at approximately one event per hour. Our results establish a practical and extensible method to identify quasiparticle bursts in superconducting circuits, as well as their correlations and spatial structure, advancing routes to suppress correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors.
items.author: Simon Sundelin, Linus Andersson, Hampus Brunander, Simone Gasparinetti

items.title: Strain-Engineered Deterministic Quantum Dots for Telecom O-Band Emission Using Buried Stressors
items.summary: Abstract The deterministic realization of quantum light sources operating at telecom wavelengths is essential for long-distance fiber-based quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate that telecom O-band emission can be achieved from site-controlled InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots (QDs). Our concept utilizes a buried AlAs/AlOx stressor layer with the unique feature of inducing a well-defined and controllable tensile strain field at the growth surface, enabling both site-selective nucleation at the mesa’s centers and a redshift of QD emission to the ∼1.3 μm wavelength range. This concept not only eliminates the need for strain-reducing layers (SRLs), which are known to degrade optical coherence, but also provides spatial control and spectral tunability. The grown telecom QDs show single-photon emission with g(2)(0) = (5.0 ± 1.0) × 10–2 at 4 K and (2.8 ± 0.3) × 10–1 at 77 K, demonstrating the quantum nature and thermal stability of the emitters. The emission characteristics of complex excitonic states are analyzed using 8-band k·p and configuration-interaction modeling, which quantitatively reproduces the experimental observations. Finally, we present a theory-supported strategy to further redshift the emission toward the center of the O-band and beyond by employing a multiburied stressor approach. This combined framework of experiment and theory establishes the buried stressor concept as a scalable route toward highly coherent, position-controlled O-band quantum emitters compatible with scalable photonic integration.
items.author: Imad Limame, Ching‐Wen Shih, Kartik Gaur, Martin Podhorský et al.

items.title: Bootstrapping symmetries in quantum many-body systems from the cross spectral form factor
items.summary: Symmetries play a central role in quantum many-body physics, yet uncovering them systematically remains challenging. We introduce a bootstrap framework to reconstruct the representation theory of hidden finite group symmetries of quantum many-body lattice Hamiltonians, using only a known symmetry subgroup $N$ and spectral correlations between its sectors. We introduce the cross spectral form factor (xSFF) as a subgroup-resolved diagnostic of hidden symmetry, computed via exact diagonalization to seed the bootstrap. Applying constraints from these data alongside the algebraic conditions of the fusion rules, our bootstrap sharply restricts candidate groups $G$. Without prior assumptions about $G$, our method can systematically recover its representation-theoretic data, including the number and dimensions of irreducible representations, their branching rules with respect to $N$, the fusion algebra, and the full character table. This framework applies to chaotic and integrable systems and accommodates unitary and anti-unitary symmetries. Through examples, we demonstrate that $G$ can be uniquely identified. Our bootstrap recovers the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ symmetry at the self-dual point of the three-state quantum torus chain, detects signatures of projective representations in the effective Hamiltonian of the driven Bose-Hubbard model, and rediscovers the $η$-pairing $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ symmetry of the one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Leveraging the universal random-matrix ramp in chaotic systems, we demonstrate the possibility of ramp-only bootstrap alongside an example with hidden commuting symmetries. We establish the xSFF as a diagnostic for conserved order parameters in a symmetry-breaking spin-$1$ chain and introduce an ancilla-assisted measurement circuit for experimental r

items.title: From BV-BFV Quantization to Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants
items.summary: We propose a program for bridging the gap between the perturbative BV-BFV quantization of Chern–Simons theory and the non-perturbative Reshetikhin–Turaev (RT) invariants of 3-manifolds, passing through factorization homology of [Formula: see text]-algebras and the derived algebraic geometry of character stacks. We conjecture that the modular tensor category underlying the RT construction arises as the [Formula: see text]-category from BV-BFV quantization of Chern–Simons theory on the disk, with the derived character stack [Formula: see text] of the complexified group and its shifted symplectic structure mediating the proposed identification. A recurring theme is the mismatch between the compact gauge group of Chern–Simons theory and the reductive algebraic group of derived algebraic geometry: we work throughout with [Formula: see text] and indicate where a Riemann–Hilbert type comparison is needed to return to the compact theory. We formulate a main conjecture asserting natural equivalence of the BV-BFV and RT constructions as [Formula: see text]-extended topological quantum field theories, together with several auxiliary conjectures and two questions, develop a proof strategy via deformation quantization of shifted symplectic stacks, and clarify the role of [Formula: see text]-Koszul duality, which relates the perturbative expansion around a flat connection to the local geometry of the character stack. We relate the perturbative expansions to the sheaf of vanishing cycles on the character stack of a [Formula: see text]-manifold, propose that a stratification of the character stack by stabilizer type organizes the trans-series decomposition, and propose that the Stokes data of the perturbative expansion should be read as a stability datum in the sense of Kontsevich–Soib

items.title: The Structure of Reality: Recognition, Necessity, and Physical Prediction
items.summary: A comparison is a physical occurrence. It needs something to compare, an operation that uses both terms, and a state in which its result can matter to what happens next. If the result is measured, the measurement needs a reference. If it is retained, the record needs a carrier. If the operation transfers energy, that energy must appear in the same account. This book asks how much of physical structure is fixed by those demands. Recognition Science begins with the distinctions already exhibited by actual operations and follows their consequences. Its central arguments remove alternatives: a conserved comparison selects a quadratic reading; its residual and reference fix a normalized cost; preservation of additive comparisons, together with a first costly join, fixes golden scaling. A retained linking observation selects three spatial dimensions under its stated realization conditions. Further constructions ask how the resulting source evolves, transfers energy and leaves records. The argument is technical because the alternatives matter. A theorem that selects one cost from a specified class says exactly which other costs fail and why. Changing the class can change the conclusion. A Hamiltonian that acts on a full field carrier establishes more than a finite matrix calculation, while an exact matrix compression remains useful at its own scope. The reader should be able to identify the physical objects, inspect the hypotheses and follow the reason for each conclusion.

items.title: Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) and Scalable Quantum Photonic Integrated Circuits: Cryogenic Quantum Light Sources, Multiplexed Readout Architectures, and Quantum Key Distribution
items.summary: Optical quantum information processing, quantum key distribution (QKD), and linear optical quantum computing (LOQC) rely fundamentally on single-photon detectors capable of ultra-high system detection efficiency, low dark count rates, sub-nanosecond timing jitter, and high maximum count rates. Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) have emerged as the gold-standard quantum light detection technology, outperforming semiconductor avalanche photodiodes (APDs) and transition-edge sensors (TES) across every major performance metric. By biasing ultrathin superconducting nanometric strips (e.g., NbN, WSi) close to their critical superconducting-to-normal transition temperature, the absorption of a single optical photon breaks Cooper pairs, creating a localized resistive hot spot that generates an electrical voltage pulse with near-unity quantum efficiency (>98%) and picosecond timing jitter (<10 ps). Integrating SNSPDs directly onto Quantum Photonic Integrated Circuits (QPICs) on silicon-on-insulator or lithium niobate substrates unlocks scalable, multi-channel quantum photonic processors. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of SNSPD-integrated quantum photonic integrated circuits. items.title: Flat Chern bands and correlated states in spiral magnet
items.summary: Flat topological bands provide a promising platform for realizing exotic correlated quantum phases such as fractional Chern insulators. Here, we predict the van der Waals monolayer ReAg 2 Cl 6 hosts isolated flat Chern bands at the Fermi level in its 120 ∘ antiferromagnetic ground state. Their flatness and nontrivial topology arise from the interplay between coplanar spin order and strong spin-orbit coupling within Re 5 d orbitals, providing a mechanism distinct from moiré systems. The spiral spin texture naturally enlarges the unit cell, reducing carrier densities while preserving sizable interaction scales. Many-body calculations show that fractional fillings of the flat bands can stabilize correlated phases, including fractional Chern insulators and charge-density-wave states. Moreover, the mechanism is generic to a broad family of Re-based compounds, with both spin configuration and flat band topology electrically tunable. These findings establish Re-based coplanar antiferromagnets as a robust, tunable, and experimentally accessible platform for flat Chern bands and correlated topological phases potentially at elevated temperatures.

items.title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
items.summary: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the Spin-Adapted Antisymmetrization Method (SAAM), a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo (NNQMC), SAAM leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated system with neural network orbitals. Compared with existing treatments of spin in NNQMC, SAAM is more accurate and efficient, achieving exact spin purity without any additional tunable hyperparameters. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we apply SAAM to study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe$_2$S$_2$] and [Fe$_4$S$_4$] clusters, offering new insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish SAAM as a robust, hyperparameter-free standard for spin-adapted NNQMC, particularly for strongly correlated systems.

items.title: Photonic Neuromorphic Processing With Coupled Spiking Silicon Microrings
items.summary: ABSTRACT Understanding the physical computing mechanisms of individual network nodes is essential for scaling neuromorphic photonic architectures. This work proposes a compact passive nonlinear photonic core based on a side‐coupled integrated spaced sequence of resonators (SCISSOR) comprising three nominally equal microrings and investigate its computing capabilities. Its nonlinearities and internal feedback enable analogue, spiking, and bistable responses that are accessed by tuning the injection power and wavelength. Implemented as a single nonlinear node in a time‐multiplexed reservoir computing, the SCISSOR achieves error‐free classification on the Iris dataset and accuracies above 97 on the Sonar task, using both analogue and digital reservoir representations with 150 virtual nodes. In the digital scheme, spiking dynamics naturally generate sparse reservoir states, enabling efficient classification even with a single spike. Intriguingly, operating points at the boundaries where sharp transitions in dynamical complexity and/or output power occur support high task‐performance, opening novel strategies for future on‐chip training. Spiking and thermal bistabilities also participate to enhance the computational performance. These results suggest that coupled optical microrings can serve as compact, physically interpretable nonlinear building blocks for future neuromorphic photonic processors, particularly in optical‐domain preprocessing and sensing scenarios where kHz‐to‐MHz signal bandwidths are relevant.

items.title: Can DFT-Trained Neural Network Potentials Reproduce Structure, Solvation, and Water-Exchange Properties in Aqueous Magnesium Solutions?
items.summary: Abstract Magnesium ions play an essential role in many biological processes but remain challenging to model in biomolecular simulations. Despite considerable scientific effort, classical force fields fail to simultaneously reproduce key structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic solution properties, likely due to their inability to explicitly account for quantum many-body effects. Here, we develop and systematically benchmark MACE neural network potentials (NNPs) for aqueous MgCl2 solutions, trained on revPBE-D3/zd and revPBE0-D3/zd density functional theory reference data, and assess their ability to reproduce a broad range of experimental solution properties including the structure of the first hydration shell, diffusion coefficient, activity derivative, water-exchange rate, and mechanism as well as solvation free energy. Both NNPs accurately reproduce the octahedral structure of the first hydration shell, ion-pairing properties, and diffusion coefficients. Combining the NNPs with transition path sampling and other enhanced sampling techniques allows us to capture the rare event of water exchange in the first hydration shell of Mg2+, revealing a dissociative exchange mechanism. Transition interface sampling yields exchange rates within 1 order of magnitude of experiment, representing a substantial improvement over classical dissociative force fields. In contrast, the NNP-derived solvation free energy significantly underestimates the experimental value, revealing a limitation of the present local NNP architecture for describing ion solvation thermodynamics. items.title: Neuro‐Driven Mechanically Programmable Metasurface for Electromagnetic Environment‐Illusion Generation
items.summary: ABSTRACT Invisibility cloaks are evolving beyond passive scattering suppression toward the active control of radar perception. However, on‐demand generation of electromagnetic environment illusions remains challenging. Passive metasurfaces are fixed after fabrication, whereas electrically reconfigurable metasurfaces usually require dense bias networks and continuous electrical holding power, which complicate large‐aperture integration and introduce steady‐state energy consumption. Here, we report an X‐band neuro‐driven mechanically programmable metasurface (NMPM) that generates prescribed electromagnetic signatures through mechanically retained coding states. To map target scattering profiles onto implementable mechanical configurations, we develop a calibration‐assisted, physics‐guided neural programming framework. This framework compensates for coupling‐induced model mismatch and addresses the non‐unique inverse mapping from desired electromagnetic responses to discrete array states. The generated states are physically written by rotating reflective meta‐atoms optimized for linearly polarized illumination, allowing the programmed configuration to be retained without continuous electrical bias. Microwave experiments on two representative target environments demonstrate that the NMPM reproduces the dominant main‐lobe directions and overall sidelobe envelopes of the target scattering profiles. Quantitative measurements yield cosine similarities of 94%–98%, with consistent agreement under the tested incidence‐angle and frequency variations. These results demonstrate a mechanically retained and algorithmically calibrated route toward adaptive radar deception, electromagnetic scene engineering, and reconfigurable sensing architectures.

items.title: Weak Measurement for Characterizing Effective Jones Matrices of Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
items.summary: ABSTRACT Pancharatnam‐Berry phase gradients generated by spatially rotated meta atoms are widely used to control optical wavefronts with metasurfaces. Here, we develop a weak measurement method for characterizing the effective Jones matrix parameters of fabricated PB phase gradient metasurfaces. In the specified effective Jones model, the local polarization response is described by the amplitude ratio and phase difference, while the spatial rotation of the meta atoms determines the PB phase gradient. By scanning the imaginary part angle and real part angle, the spin dependent deflection is converted into a two dimensional centroid map. The amplitude ratio, phase difference, and phase gradient produce different spatial features in this map, providing information for their distinction and retrieval. For a fabricated metasurface with a known phase gradient, the amplitude ratio and phase difference are obtained by fitting the measured centroid response with the theoretical model. When all three parameters are unknown, three independently trained machine learning models retrieve the amplitude ratio, phase difference, and phase gradient from the same complete centroid map and its angular coordinates. These results establish two dimensional weak measurement as an optical approach for characterizing the effective parameters of PB phase gradient metasurfaces.
